item.title: BlackRock expands AI push with new robotics ETF as investor enthusiasm cools
item.description: BlackRock has launched a new robotics focused ETF as investors become more selective about AI investments. The fund targets companies using intelligent machines across industries such as manufacturing and transportation, adding to a rapidly expanding market of ETFs built around different parts of the AI theme.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: BlackRock has added another AI focused exchange traded fund to its growing lineup, turning to robotics as investors become more selective about where they place their bets on the technology theme, according to Reuters.The global asset manager launched the iShares Future Robotics and Related Technologies ETF on Wednesday, targeting companies that use intelligent machines to automate repetitive tasks across industries including transportation and manufacturing.Robotics seen as next leg of AI adoptionBlackRock sees robotics as an important part of the next phase of AI adoption, with intelligent machines potentially extending the technology's reach beyond software and data centres into a wider range of industries.The new fund comes as investors' enthusiasm for AI has encountered bouts of volatility. BlackRock US head of equity ETFs Jay Jacobs said the recent swings showed that AI exposure is becoming a more complicated investment theme, Reuters reported.“Recent volatility is a reminder that AI is not a single trade and that investors need to be deliberate about where and how they take exposure, Jacobs said.He added that the volatility had not changed BlackRock's conviction in the broader AI theme.AI ETF market keeps expandingThe new fund also adds to an increasingly crowded market of ETFs built around the AI investment story. Investors already have access to scores of ETFs explicitly tracking AI, alongside technology focused funds with significant exposure to major AI linked companies such as Nvidia and Micron, according to Reuters.At least six AI linked ETFs have launched over the past month, with several targeting specific corners of the industry rather than taking a broad approach.Global X recently introduced the LLM ETF, focused on companies developing large language models, while Defiance launched an ETF targeting bonds issued by AI infrastructure companies, Reuters reported.Jacobs said expectations around AI can change quickly, while adoption may develop unevenly and market risk remains concentrated among a relatively narrow group of companies.“Expectations can shift quickly, adoption can develop unevenly and market risk remains concentrated in a relatively narrow group of companies, he said.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: US Treasury yields slip as AI concerns boost safe haven demand ahead of 20 year auction
item.description: US Treasury yields slipped as investors weighed the impact of higher borrowing costs on AI stocks, with the 10 year yield heading for a second straight daily decline. The move came ahead of a $13 billion 20 year Treasury auction, while markets continued to price in a muted chance of a Fed rate hike.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: US Treasury yields slipped on Wednesday as investors weighed the impact of higher borrowing costs on AI related stocks, while the market awaited a $13 billion auction of 20 year bonds later in the day, according to a Reuters report.The move came as recent swings in AI stocks continued to influence the bond market. Concerns over the heavy spending needed to build AI infrastructure have raised questions about how higher interest rates could affect companies such as CoreWeave. When those concerns weigh on equities, investors have at times shifted towards Treasuries, pushing yields lower.The benchmark 10 year Treasury yield fell 1.5 basis points to 5.102%, putting it on track for a second consecutive daily decline. The 30 year yield slipped 1.2 basis points to 5.413%, while the 2 year yield declined 0.9 basis point to 4.778%.AI volatility keeps bond investors alertUS stocks were slightly higher on Wednesday, helped by a surge in SpaceX shares after its quarterly results eased some concerns around the AI sector. CoreWeave shares, however, fell, highlighting the uneven reaction among AI linked stocks. There has been a very clear trade off across capital markets in almost a risk on, risk off rotation where equities will draw down and we'll see flows in and out of the Treasury market, said Bill Northey, senior investment director at U.S. Bank Wealth Management, Billings, Montana, according to Reuters.Northey said the 10 year Treasury yield at 5.1% was also becoming competitive with equities for investors seeking returns in fixed income.Fed hike bets remain subduedThe bond market's move lower in yields came despite hotter than expected inflation readings. Markets are pricing in a 14.9% chance of a 25 basis point Fed rate hike at the October 28 policy meeting, down from 33.2% a week ago and 57.6% a month earlier, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Treasury supply is also in focus, with the US government set to auction $13 billion of 20 year bonds on Wednesday and $26 billion of five year TIPS on Thursday.The 10 year yield has already fallen 14.6 basis points this week, its biggest weekly decline in eight months, after AI related concerns triggered a broader equity selloff and drove investors towards safer assets, according to Reuters.
